assessment: The incumbent combines selection, removable assembly, order checking and a layout diagram, plausibly reducing customer construction work while retaining rearrangeability. Performance misses the time target (11-minute median); seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. Five reported partition problems warrant investigation but do not establish five verified packing errors. Repeated three-compartment orders taking seven to nine minutes support retaining the basic process; mixed batches containing every extreme delay suggest switching or complexity, without separating them. A concrete limit on a dimensional explanation is D2-O5: measured widths overlap between successful and retried insertions, so width alone is not an established cause. Neither proposed opening establishes pilot success.

openings.claim: Order-specific staging and a component tally may reduce searching, selection errors and repeated checking in mixed-layout work.
openings.delta: Add a reusable staging area keyed to the accepted layout and exterior color before the existing insertion and packing steps.
openings.prediction: Compared with the incumbent, matched mixed orders show less selection/checking time and fewer verified component discrepancies; unchanged insertion time would localize the benefit.
openings.probe: Use six reusable sample sets within the 15-sample allowance. Alternate baseline and staged runs across workers, balancing layout and color. Time each stage, including staging, and independently reconcile packed components against the order. Compare identical layouts across methods.
assumptions: Measured preparation and trial time fit the fixed delivery schedule.
Initial spending stays at most 500 and recurring material increase at most 0.40 per order.

openings.claim: Some customer difficulty may come from mapping the short partition to the ordered layout even when the supplied parts are correct.
openings.delta: Replace the generic three-layout diagram with an order-specific diagram identifying the short partition and its slot.
openings.prediction: With verified identical contents, the specific diagram reduces short-partition placement errors and requests for help.
openings.probe: Allocate the ten participants evenly between diagrams, balancing ordered layouts. Record unaided completion, placement errors and time. Treat results as directional evidence, not proof of the 90% pilot target.
assumptions: Participants can test without prior exposure to the alternative diagram.
Diagram preparation and printing fit the remaining shared budget and delivery time.
Product geometry, removable joints, assortment, accepted counts and colors remain unchanged.
